runs.message: Make a late-night mix: atmospheric electronic music and trip-hop, a little dark and spacious, no rock or festival EDM.
runs.name: After Hours
runs.reply: Here's your late-night mix: a slow, spacious arc of atmospheric electronic and trip-hop that opens in the dark, builds through the trip-hop heart, and dissolves into ambient stillness. No rock, no festival EDM — all low-energy, reverb-heavy, headphone-friendly. 1) Portishead – Wandering Star (53 BPM): the definitive Bristol trip-hop sound, a lonely half-time groove with processed vocals sets the dark, spacious tone. 2) Massive Attack – Inertia Creeps (Alpha Mix) (85 BPM): keeps the trip-hop pulse but leans into dark, hypnotic, sample-based atmosphere. 3) Archive – Man-Made (56 BPM): warm, dark synth textures and a minimal beat for the quiet, introspective core. 4) Lamb – Darkness (90 BPM): the emotional center — dark, dreamy, intimate vocals over layered synths. 5) Hooverphonic – Inhaler (58 BPM): a sensual, hypnotic mid-90s cut adding warmer, more human color. 6) UNKLE – Nursery Rhyme, Breather (67 BPM): eerie, cinematic, introspective, bridging into the instrumental turn. 7) Boards of Canada – Over the Horizon Radar (93 BPM): serene yet eerie with a spacious, open texture — the 'spacious' requirement at its purest. 8) Jamie xx – The Rest Is Noise (63 BPM): a dark, hypnotic ambient close that dissolves into stillness. The order descends gently into the small hours. I kept variety by using one Portishead track and skipping the Enigma/DJ Shadow options; happy to swap in DJ Shadow – Stem or Enigma – Sadeness for a grittier or choral flavor, or end more ambient with Emancipator – Outlaw.
runs.guidance: Prefers late-night atmospheric electronic and trip-hop: dark, spacious, low-energy, reverb-heavy, headphone-friendly. Explicitly excludes rock and festival EDM. Values variety across artists and a thoughtful slow arc (trip-hop core into ambient close).
